goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

That fallback would indeed drop any contextual attributes injected into the context (e.g., via log.WithContextualAttributes in the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware), but the diff alone doesn’t prove that `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` can ever return a non-*log.ConcreteLogger in this codepath. So it’s a real robustness/edge-case concern, not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext is only applied in QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics (contextual_logger_middleware.go), while SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream simply call m.next.* without enriching the context. Since LoggerMiddleware now relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) for contextual attributes (logger_middleware.go), stream-related requests will not carry the same plugin/request attributes as the other endpoints, making logging/instrumentation inconsistent. This is a concrete, diff-grounded completeness issue, but it affects observability rather than core correctness.

At the same time, `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` removes explicit inclusion of `pluginId`/`endpoint`/`ds*`/`uname` and instead relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` to emit those via contextual logging. No tests are added/updated in this diff to verify that these attributes actually reach the final "Plugin Request Completed" log line or that `FromContext`/fallback paths work, making this a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly added behavior.

The log line now uses m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), but the diff does not show that plog.Logger.FromContext (or the underlying infra logger) will automatically include trace info as a field, so this change plausibly drops trace-log correlation for these log lines even if tracing is still in the context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface silently breaks every implementer not updated by this diff; no evidence all other plog.Logger implementers were enumerated and updated

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new required method `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` to the exported `Logger` interface in `pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go`. Any other `plog.Logger` implementations elsewhere in the codebase (not shown in this diff) would need to be updated to compile. The diff only updates `TestLogger` (`fake.go`) and `grafanaInfraLogWrapper` (`logger.go`), so the review concern about potentially missing implementers is grounded, but the diff alone cannot prove that other implementers exist or that the build is broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing logger_middleware_test.go not updated in the diff despite the log-attribute contract changing; either it now fails on removed attributes or it never asserted them, leaving the new attribute set unpinned by tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the logging attribute mechanism: LoggerMiddleware no longer appends pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID directly into logParams (those lines were removed), and instead logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` while a new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is introduced to inject `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` into the context (`instrumentContext` -> `log.WithContextualAttributes`). No tests are added/updated in this diff to assert the new contract (that attributes come from context and that the new middleware is required/ordered correctly), so it’s a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage/contract pinning rather than a definite functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SubscribeStream, PublishStream, and RunStream pass through without instrumentContext, so streaming plugin logs carry no endpoint/pluginId/user context (advisory, pre-existing)

adjudication.rationale: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only calls instrumentContext() for QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics, but SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream simply delegate to m.next without enriching the context (pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go). Since LoggerMiddleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), streaming requests will lack endpoint/pluginId/user attributes in the logger context. This is a real, diff-grounded incompleteness in the new contextual-logging approach (also consistent with it being pre-existing behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext falls back to d.New() when the type assertion to *log.ConcreteLogger fails, silently discarding contextual attributes instead of surfacing the invariant violation (advisory)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext calls d.l.FromContext(ctx) and type-asserts to *log.ConcreteLogger; on failure it returns d.New() (no error/log), which will drop any contextual attributes derived from ctx. The fallback behavior is real and diff-grounded, but whether the assertion must always succeed (and thus should be surfaced) isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, so it’s more of an edge-case/invariant-handling concern than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go:14 — Scope drift: chore/rename PR adds new exported method FromContext to Logger interface, breaking all existing implementers of plog.Logger across the codebase (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new exported method `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` to the `Logger` interface in `pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go`, which is an API/scope expansion beyond a pure rename and is source-breaking for any existing `plog.Logger` implementers not updated. The diff updates two implementers (`TestLogger` in `pkg/plugins/log/fake.go` and `grafanaInfraLogWrapper` in `pkg/plugins/log/logger.go`), but it’s not verifiable from this diff alone that *all* other implementers across the repo are handled—so the core concern is real (breaking interface change), but the “all implementers” claim can’t be confirmed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go — Scope drift: new ContextualLoggerMiddleware added under a rename-chore title, changing grafana-data-egress log field provenance; middleware-stack ordering dependency (ContextualLogger above LoggerMiddleware) is an unstated, unenforced invariant (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does more than a rename: it introduces a new middleware (pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go) and changes logging behavior in LoggerMiddleware. LoggerMiddleware.logRequest no longer appends plugin/request fields (pluginId, endpoint, dsName/dsUID, uname, traceID) and instead logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), relying on contextual attributes being present in ctx. Those attributes are now injected by ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext via log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, ...). In CreateMiddlewares, this dependency is satisfied only by ordering (NewContextualLoggerMiddleware() placed before NewLoggerMiddleware(...)), and nothing in code enforces that invariant if the stack order changes. This is a real, diff-grounded scope/architecture concern, but not an immediate defect given the current ordering in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: logger_middleware.go:49-57 — traceID removed from logParams and not added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware's instrumentContext, so traceID only appears if infra logger's FromContext injects it, risking loss of trace correlation in grafana-data-egress events (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In logger_middleware.go the explicit traceID enrichment was removed (tracing import and TraceIDFromContext block), and logParams no longer include "traceID". The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext only adds endpoint/pluginId/ds/user attributes via log.WithContextualAttributes and does not add trace ID. The only remaining way for trace correlation to appear in the emitted "Plugin Request Completed" log is via plog.Logger.FromContext(ctx) / infra logger behavior, which is not shown in this diff. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability regression risk, but whether it is an actual defect depends on unverified FromContext behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: contextual_logger_middleware.go:57-68 — SubscribeStream, PublishStream, and RunStream are bare pass-throughs, so stream-related plugin logs lack pluginId/endpoint/uname contextual attributes, enforced inconsistently (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go, instrumentContext(...) is applied in QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics, but SubscribeStream (lines ~57-59), PublishStream (~61-63), and RunStream (~65-67) directly delegate to m.next without calling instrumentContext. Given the middleware’s stated purpose (“adds a contextual logger to the request context”), this creates an inconsistent scope where stream-related requests won’t get the plugin/request/user attributes in context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:47-49 — TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger disconnected from f, so assertions on FromContext-based logging never record calls, producing silently-passing tests (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go the newly added `(*TestLogger).FromContext` ignores the receiver and always returns `NewTestLogger()`. Any code that does `f.FromContext(ctx).Info/...` will record logs on the new logger instance, not on `f`’s `InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs`, breaking the expected semantics of a contextual/derived logger and making assertions against the injected `TestLogger` incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:47-53 — grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext falls back to d.New() when type-assert to *log.ConcreteLogger fails, discarding all contextual attributes set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx) calls d.l.FromContext(ctx) but if the result is not a *log.ConcreteLogger it falls back to return d.New(), which does not use the provided context.Context at all. Given the Logger interface contract added in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go (“FromContext … plus the given context”), this fallback would drop any contextual attributes placed into ctx (e.g., via ContextualLoggerMiddleware’s log.WithContextualAttributes), so the finding is diff-grounded and represents incorrect behavior in that branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go:23-40 — Mechanical interface{} → any rewrite of PrettyLogger signatures is unrelated formatting churn inflating the diff of a Chore PR (P3)

adjudication.rationale: The cited change in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go is a mechanical Go 1.18+ modernization from `...interface{}` to `...any` in PrettyLogger (and Logger) method signatures. This is a stylistic/type-alias rewrite and not a verifiable defect or substantive issue from the diff alone; whether it is “unrelated churn” depends on PR intent/scope, which is not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TraceID silently dropped from the grafana-data-egress log event: migration to contextual logging via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info() no longer appends traceID, losing trace correlation for Plugin Request Completed events

adjudication.rationale: In `logger_middleware.go`, the previous explicit enrichment with `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and `logParams = append(logParams, "traceID", traceID)` was removed, and the log now uses `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` with `logParams` that no longer include `traceID`. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`’s `instrumentContext` adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, datasource, and `uname`, but does not add any trace identifier. Nothing in the diff shows `FromContext` or `WithContextualAttributes` automatically appending a traceID field to this log event, so the diff verifiably drops the `traceID` key from the emitted fields for "Plugin Request Completed".

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger(), so logs emitted through FromContext are invisible to tests holding the original fake — tests asserting on InfoLogs/Calls get zero recorded calls and contextual attributes are dropped

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go, TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() (a fresh instance) instead of returning a logger that records into the same TestLogger. Call sites updated to use FromContext(ctx).Info(...) (e.g., LoggerMiddleware) will therefore write to a different TestLogger than the one held by the test, so assertions on f.InfoLogs/Calls can observe zero calls and any contextual enrichment is effectively lost for the original fake.

adjudication_records.issue_text: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently falls back to d.New() when the infra logger is not a *log.ConcreteLogger, discarding all contextual attributes (pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname, endpoint) with no error

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx) does `concreteInfraLogger, ok := d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)` and on failure returns `d.New()` with no use of `ctx`. The Logger interface contract added in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go says FromContext should return a logger contextualized by the provided context; falling back to New() drops any context-based attributes (e.g., those added via log.WithContextualAttributes in the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware) and does so silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: LoggerMiddleware has a hidden, unenforced ordering dependency on ContextualLoggerMiddleware appearing earlier in CreateMiddlewares; reusing it elsewhere or reordering the slice produces egress events missing all identifying fields with no test/compile signal

adjudication.rationale: In `logger_middleware.go`, `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` no longer appends identifying fields like `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName/dsUID`, `uname`, or `traceID` to `logParams`; instead it logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is the only code in this diff that enriches `ctx` with those attributes (`instrumentContext` -> `log.WithContextualAttributes`). `CreateMiddlewares` currently places `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` before `NewLoggerMiddleware(...)`, but this dependency is implicit and not enforced by types/tests; reordering or reusing `LoggerMiddleware` without the contextual middleware would silently produce logs missing those fields. However, with the shown ordering, no defect is demonstrated in the diff itself—it's a real maintainability/ordering-coupling concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of recording into f, so logs emitted through FromContext are silently discarded and tests using TestLogger fail or pass vacuously

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/plugins/log/fake.go`, the newly added `TestLogger.FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger` returns `NewTestLogger()` rather than returning `f` (or a logger sharing `f`'s backing storage). Callers like `LoggerMiddleware` now do `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so when `m.logger` is a `*TestLogger`, the log call records into an unreachable fresh logger instance, effectively discarding logs and making tests that inspect the original `TestLogger` pass/fail vacuously.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The grafana-data-egress log line permanently loses endpoint, pluginId, uname, dsName, dsUID, and traceID from its logParams, losing data-egress attribution with no equivalent elsewhere in the diff

adjudication.rationale: The removed fields (endpoint, pluginId, uname, dsName, dsUID) are not necessarily lost: the diff adds `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` which injects those attributes into the `context.Context` via `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, p)` (see `instrumentContext` in `contextual_logger_middleware.go`), and `CreateMiddlewares` places this middleware before `NewLoggerMiddleware`. `LoggerMiddleware` then logs using `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, which is explicitly intended to pick up context-derived attributes. While `traceID` is no longer appended in `LoggerMiddleware`, the finding’s claim that there is “no equivalent elsewhere in the diff” is false for the other attribution fields, and the traceID behavior cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If the infra logger fails the *log.ConcreteLogger type assertion in FromContext, the d.New() fallback drops all contextual attributes and no error is surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx) does `d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)` and on failure returns `d.New()` with no args. That fallback does not incorporate any attributes stored in the provided context (it creates a new logger without using ctx), contradicting the interface contract added in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go (`FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` “has this logger's context plus the given context”). No error/logging is emitted, so contextual attributes can be silently dropped if the type assertion fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Correct middleware ordering (NewContextualLoggerMiddleware outside NewLoggerMiddleware) is undocumented and unenforced; the old InstrumentationMiddleware comment about middleware stack position was deleted rather than moved, so future reordering silently reintroduces attribute loss

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes LoggerMiddleware to rely on context enrichment via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go), and moves the enrichment logic into a new `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` that calls `log.WithContextualAttributes` (contextual_logger_middleware.go). In CreateMiddlewares, the new middleware is currently placed before `NewLoggerMiddleware` (pluginsintegration.go), so behavior is correct now, but the required ordering is not enforced anywhere and the prior warning comment in InstrumentationMiddleware about needing to be "at the top of the middleware stack" was removed rather than moved. A future reorder could silently drop endpoint/plugin/user/datasource attributes from logs without any compile-time signal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: FromContext silently downcasts to *log.ConcreteLogger with a lossy, invisible fallback; the any return type makes the assertion fragile to upstream changes like future logger wrapping

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx) does a concrete type assertion: `d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)`. If upstream changes return a different logger implementation/wrapper, this will fail and silently fall back to `d.New()` (dropping the contextual logger coming from `FromContext`). That’s not a guaranteed current defect from the diff alone, but it is a diff-grounded robustness/maintenance concern created by the new method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ContextualLoggerMiddleware duplicates the instrumentContext field list and the Logger interface now has FromContext as a near-duplicate of New(ctx ...any), creating two parallel hand-maintained mechanisms for deriving a contextual logger

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two overlapping ways to derive a contextual logger: Logger now has both `New(ctx ...any) Logger` and the newly added `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` (see `pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go`), and the middleware now relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` (`logger_middleware.go`) while contextual attributes are injected separately via `log.WithContextualAttributes` in `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (`contextual_logger_middleware.go`). That creates parallel mechanisms that must be kept consistent. However, the claim that `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` “duplicates the instrumentContext field list” is not strictly supported by this diff alone, because the prior `instrumentContext` implementation was removed from the renamed metrics middleware; in the shown changes it exists only in the new middleware.

adjudication_records.issue_text: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-assertion fallback returning d.New() on non-*log.ConcreteLogger silently drops contextual log attributes

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/plugins/log/logger.go`, `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` does `d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)` and, if the type assertion fails, returns `d.New()` with no args. That fallback does not incorporate the provided `context.Context`, so any contextual attributes expected from `FromContext(ctx)` would be lost in that path (i.e., `FromContext` would not fulfill its contract).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Diff removes traceID attribute from LoggerMiddleware.logRequest logging, potentially regressing log-trace correlation if the infra logger does not re-derive trace correlation from the span in ctx

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes adding `traceID` to `logParams` in `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` by deleting the `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` logic and the `infra/tracing` import, and now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. While a new `FromContext(ctx)` method is introduced on the logger wrapper, the diff does not show that it re-adds `traceID` as a structured field, so log-trace correlation via an explicit `traceID` attribute may be lost depending on the underlying logger implementation. This is a concrete, diff-grounded potential regression, but not provably a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Functional coupling: ContextualLoggerMiddleware must wrap LoggerMiddleware in the correct order for the new FromContext path to see contextual attributes, which cannot be confirmed as correctly wired from the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the wiring/order: in `CreateMiddlewares` the new `clientmiddleware.NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()` is inserted immediately before `clientmiddleware.NewLoggerMiddleware(...)` (and after tracing/metrics). Since `LoggerMiddleware` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, the context enrichment from `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (which calls `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, p)`) is explicitly positioned to happen before `LoggerMiddleware` runs. The finding’s claim that this “cannot be confirmed as correctly wired from the diff” misreads what is visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has zero test coverage; the entire attribute-injection contract (instrumentContext, DataSourceInstanceSettings/User branches, endpoint tag, which methods inject vs don't) is untested, risking silent loss of log fields in future refactors

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new middleware file `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go` with nontrivial logic (`instrumentContext` builds an attributes slice with conditional branches for `DataSourceInstanceSettings` and `User`, and only certain client methods call it). The only related test change shown is renaming `instrumentation_middleware_test.go` to `metrics_middleware_test.go`, and the contextual-logger-enrichment logic was explicitly removed from the metrics middleware (no longer calling `instrumentContext`). There is no new/updated test in the diff that exercises `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` or validates the injected fields/method coverage, so the finding about zero test coverage for this new attribute-injection contract is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger() unconnected to the receiver, so LoggerMiddleware tests asserting on the injected fake see zero calls and cannot verify the new FromContext logging path, creating false confidence

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/plugins/log/fake.go`, `TestLogger.FromContext` is implemented as `return NewTestLogger()`, which discards the receiver and returns a brand-new logger instance. Since `LoggerMiddleware` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, any caller using `TestLogger` and asserting against the originally injected `TestLogger`'s `InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs` will see zero calls because the log call lands on the new instance instead. This makes the fake/logger behavior inconsistent with expectations for contextual loggers (it should typically return the same logger or a wrapper that still records into the same underlying sink).

adjudication_records.issue_text: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext's !ok fallback silently returns d.New(), discarding all contextual attributes injected by ContextualLoggerMiddleware; a refactor of log.New's return type would silently strip contextual fields from logs with no test signal

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext does a concrete type assertion: `concreteInfraLogger, ok := d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)`. If that fails it falls back to `return d.New()`, which does not use the provided `context.Context` and therefore would not preserve any contextual attributes injected into the context (e.g., by the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware via `log.WithContextualAttributes`). The diff doesn’t prove the assertion can fail today (depends on what `log.New(...)` returns), but it is a real, diff-grounded robustness/maintainability concern: changing the underlying infra logger type could silently drop contextual fields without an obvious test failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The diff removes the traceID attribute from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log without replacement in the new middleware and without any test asserting traceID presence, breaking log-to-trace correlation with zero test signal

adjudication.rationale: In `logger_middleware.go`, the previous explicit trace correlation field is removed: the import of `pkg/infra/tracing` is deleted and the code that appended `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` into `logParams` is gone. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName/dsUID`, and `uname` via `log.WithContextualAttributes`, with no trace ID added. The logging call now uses `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, but nothing in the diff shows that this injects a `traceID` attribute. No tests in the shown diff assert presence of `traceID`, so this regression would be untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: grafana-data-egress log event silently loses fields: traceID, pluginId, and endpoint dropped from logRequest's logParams during instrumentation → contextual-logger migration, breaking downstream log pipelines/dashboards querying by these fields

adjudication.rationale: In `logger_middleware.go`, `logRequest` used to append `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` into `logParams`, but the tracing import and this logic were removed and no equivalent was added in the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (it only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, ds/user fields via `log.WithContextualAttributes`). So the `grafana-data-egress` log emitted by `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` will no longer include `traceID` based on what’s shown in this diff. However, the finding’s claim that `pluginId` and `endpoint` are “dropped” is not clearly true because those are now added to the context in `instrumentContext` and may still be emitted via the contextual logger.

adjudication_records.issue_text: traceID has no replacement source anywhere in the diff — the deleted tracing.TraceIDFromContext call is not compensated by instrumentContext, which only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname, and only for QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics

adjudication.rationale: In `logger_middleware.go`, the diff removes the `tracing` import and deletes the block that extracted `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and appended it to `logParams`. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware`’s `instrumentContext` only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, and `uname` via `log.WithContextualAttributes`, and there’s no trace ID enrichment shown anywhere in this diff. This appears to be an observability/telemetry regression (loss of `traceID` field in the “Plugin Request Completed” log), not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: traceID silently dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' logs; nothing in ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext or grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext re-adds it, losing trace correlation

adjudication.rationale: In `logger_middleware.go`, the previous explicit enrichment with `traceID := tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and `logParams = append(logParams, "traceID", traceID)` was removed, along with the `tracing` import. The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext` only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, datasource/user info via `log.WithContextualAttributes`, and does not add a trace ID. The log call was changed to `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, but the diff does not show any explicit traceID injection there, so trace correlation in these log lines is at least no longer guaranteed by this code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently falls back to d.New() when the wrapped logger is not a *log.ConcreteLogger, dropping all contextual attributes with no signal

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext calls d.l.FromContext(ctx) but then type-asserts it to *log.ConcreteLogger. If that assertion fails, it returns d.New() (with no args) rather than wrapping/using the logger returned by d.l.FromContext(ctx). That fallback is silent and will not preserve any contextual attributes that may have been attached to ctx via the underlying FromContext implementation, contrary to the FromContext contract added to the Logger interface.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stream endpoints (SubscribeStream, PublishStream, RunStream) are excluded from contextual logging as pure pass-throughs, so stream errors lose plugin/user identity in logs

adjudication.rationale: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware only calls instrumentContext() for QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics, while SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream are pure pass-throughs (contextual_logger_middleware.go). LoggerMiddleware also only wraps those four endpoints and now relies on logger.FromContext(ctx) for contextual fields (logger_middleware.go). Therefore, any logs emitted during stream endpoints that depend on contextual attributes in ctx will not include plugin/user/datasource identity, matching the finding as an observability gap rather than a functional defect.
